transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-09
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 1:03
Attendees: Sofia Kim (Redwood AE), Liam Ortega (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (Redwood Solutions), Maya Patel (HaloEdge CTO), Ethan Wu (HaloEdge Sec Eng), Jordan Lee (HaloEdge Legal), Amir Kahn (HaloEdge Infra)

Auto Summary: quick security intake to validate SOC2/ISO posture, KMS/HSM needs, SSO/SAML, RBAC and audit log retention requirements. Customer leaning toward Dedicated or Private; primary concerns around key custody, HSM integration, and retention for legal e-discovery.

Topics: SOC2 evidence, encryption and KMS options (customer-managed KMS vs Redwood-managed), HSM/EPKS, SSO/SAML idp integration, RBAC/SCIM, audit log retention and export, PII redaction/retention policies, network isolation (VPC/private control plane), timeline for pilot.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Sofia Kim: Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh, this is Sofia from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. Quick round-robin?
[00:05] Maya Patel: Maya here, CTO at HaloEdge. We've got Ethan, Jordan and Amir with me.
[00:10] Ethan Wu: Ethan, security engineering.
[00:11] Jordan Lee: Jordan, legal.
[00:12] Amir Kahn: Amir, infra.
[00:15] Liam Ortega: Liam, Redwood SE. I'll be the technical person on follow-ups.
[00:18] Priya Desai: Priya on solutions, hi all.
[00:20] Sofia Kim: Cool, objective for today is to walk through your security gating — SOC2, ISO questions, KMS/HSM, SSO, RBAC, and any data retention/ediscovery needs so we can sort out hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[00:33] Maya Patel: Yeah, we want to be safe about keys. For compliance we need to control KMS and ideally HSM-backed keys. We are subject to financial regs in a few states, so retention windows and auditability are big.
[00:45] Ethan Wu: Also, we have a strong requirement for SSO — SAML with our Okta setup, SCIM for provisioning, and role-based access for access segmentation.
[00:53] Jordan Lee: And legal wants data retention logs for up to seven years in certain cases — e-discovery. We know that's long, but we need an exportable chain of custody and immutable audit logs.
[01:05] Liam Ortega: Got it. High-level: Redwood Hosted supports SOC2, we can offer customer-managed KMS integration in Hosted for key wrapping, but for full HSM control and air-gapped requirements Private (VPC/on-prem) is recommended. Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and stronger network isolation but keys can be either Redwood-managed or customer-managed depending on contract.
[01:30] Amir Kahn: Quick question — when you say customer-managed KMS in Hosted, are the plaintext keys ever in Redwood land? We can't allow key material to be exportable.
[01:38] Liam Ortega: Good question. For Hosted with customer KMS we use envelope encryption: we never persist customer plaintext keys — Redwood holds a data encryption key that's itself wrapped by your KMS. But if you require HSM-backed never-exportable keys, Private with direct HSM integration is the path.
[01:53] Ethan Wu: So, envelope approach still leaves a wrapped DEK that Redwood can access if KMS allows unwrap calls — do you require calls to customer's KMS for every session?
[02:02] Liam Ortega: We can configure rewrap policies. We usually do per-instance unwrap with short-lived DEKs and cache policies that obey your policy — we can disable caching and force KMS calls per request at a cost/latency trade-off.
[02:15] Maya Patel: That latency tradeoff is important; we do not want high tail latency for real-time flows. Can you show empirical numbers?
[02:22] Sofia Kim: We'll include a short latency benchmark as part of next steps. Liam, you'll run a Dedicated config with customer KMS and compare to default caching?
[02:29] Liam Ortega: Yeah we'll put together a small test harness. Also worth flagging: Dedicated on-prem has an option to plug in an external HSM via PKCS#11 or AWS CloudHSM for key unwraps local to the cluster.
[02:43] Amir Kahn: For CloudHSM we need VPC endpoints and private routing — do you support that with Redwood Private?
[02:48] Priya Desai: Yes Private supports VPC peering, private control plane, and local KMS connectivity. We also have an on-prem package for customers that require physical air-gaps.
[02:59] Jordan Lee: About audit logs: Are audit trails write-once? Can we push them to our SIEM and retain beyond your retention? We prefer keeping copies in our S3 buckets for legal holds.
[03:10] Liam Ortega: We provide immutable append-only audit logs that can stream to customer destinations — S3, Splunk, or your SIEM — with configurable retention. We also have an export API for chain-of-custody reports. The retention inside Redwood can be set per-customer; for longer retention you should configure external archival.
[03:25] Ethan Wu: What's the schema for those logs? We need fields like request_id, user_id, model_version, tokens_count, redaction_flags.
[03:33] Liam Ortega: We include a rich schema; we'll share the log spec. Note some fields are redacted for privacy by default unless you explicitly enable full payload logging and sign an agreement.
[03:44] Maya Patel: That is a point — for PCI/PII we can't log raw prompts. We need either prompt redaction or on-demand sampling with approvals.
[03:53] Priya Desai: We have prompt redaction and filtered logging options; plus ability to enable hashed prompt fingerprints to support debugging without storing plaintext.
[04:02] Jordan Lee: On SAML/SSO provisioning — can you support multiple identity providers and scoped RBAC? We have multiple business units and need separation.
[04:09] Sofia Kim: Yes, we support multiple idps, attribute-based mappings, and hierarchical RBAC. SCIM provisioning is supported for user sync. We can show the console RBAC roles and custom role creation in the next deep-dive.
[04:23] Amir Kahn: For a pilot we want to simulate 50 QPS and mid-sized models; what's the path? Hosted will be faster to start but doesn't meet our HSM requirement. Dedicated would be an intermediate — private if we need HSM and air-gap.
[04:36] Liam Ortega: Exactly — many customers start on Hosted for quick evaluation with customer-managed KMS (with limited caching) then move to Dedicated or Private once they hit HSM/air-gap or strict latency SLAs.
[04:47] Maya Patel: OK timeline: Security team needs to sign off to start a POC. We aim to start pilot in three weeks.
[04:53] Jordan Lee: Legal will need the data processing agreement and any amendments for customer-managed keys.
[04:57] Sofia Kim: We'll send the DPA and an addendum for KMS/HSM custody options.
[05:02] Ethan Wu: One more thing — we do regular pen tests. Will you accept co-ordinated pentests and provide a safe-testing window?
[05:09] Liam Ortega: We do; we have a pen test policy and coordinated window. We'll also provide a contact and a pre-approved scope template.
[05:16] Maya Patel: Great. Anything else narrow I should call out?
[05:19] Amir Kahn: Backups — do you encrypt backups with the same KMS and can we control snapshot export?
[05:24] Priya Desai: Backups are encrypted; for Private we can ensure snapshots are stored in your environment encrypted by your KMS. For Hosted, backups are encrypted and can be wrapped with customer KMS keys depending on contract.
[05:36] Jordan Lee: For e-discovery, we need to know retention deletion semantics — hard delete vs soft delete and legal hold options.
[05:44] Liam Ortega: We support soft delete with retention windows and freeze-on-legal-hold. We'll detail the retention model in the follow-up doc.
[05:52] Sofia Kim: Ok wrapping up — recap and next steps: Sofia to share SOC2 + ISO artifacts and DPA addendum, Liam runs the Dedicated KMS latency probe, Maya to share sample prompts and expected QPS, schedule architecture deep-dive. Any other last items?
[06:05] Maya Patel: That covers it, thanks.
[06:08] Jordan Lee: Thanks all.
[06:10] Sofia Kim: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs.
[06:15] [meeting ends]

Notes: transcription contains a few mis-heard acronyms (e.g., 'Sam-el' sometimes), occasional speaker label mismatch; timestamps approximate. Links mentioned: DPA draft (link sent in chat), SOC2 report (will be shared), latency benchmark sheet (to be shared).

Action recap (verbal):
- Send SOC2, ISO mapping, pen-test summary (Sofia)
- Run Dedicated+KMS latency probe, share numbers (Liam)
- Provide prompt set + QPS (Maya)
- Schedule follow-up architecture deep-dive with Amir and Priya

End of transcript.
